trust_decision.summary: dns.name.from_wire_parser decides how many compression pointers an untrusted wire name may follow; at the pinned commit the only bound is that each pointer must point strictly backwards, so the hop count is unbounded except by message size.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names dns.name.from_wire_parser() directly, and it is the only compression-pointer decoder in the tree.

fix_sites.entry_point: dns.name.from_wire / dns.name.from_wire_parser, reached via dns.wire.Parser.get_name from dns.message.from_wire (dns/message.py:1287, question dns/message.py:1128, RR owner dns/message.py:1152) and every rdata from_wire_parser that calls parser.get_name (e.g. dns/rdtypes/ANY/SOA.py:76-77)
fix_sites.module_kind: core wire-format name decoder (library public API)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: No second decompressor: grep for pointer-masking (0x3F, seek, biggest_pointer) finds only dns/name.py:1151-1162; dns/wire.py:9-10 is a thin wrapper that delegates to it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Nothing to dismiss: every name-decoding route funnels through dns/name.py:1139, so a fix in that loop covers all of them at once.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate compressed names that follow a few chained pointers, and names whose label run continues forward past an earlier pointer target, must still decode; a chain of exactly 16 must decode to the root name (fix test). An over-strict limit (e.g. 1 hop) or forbidding pointer-to-pointer breaks real messages.

O6_input_shapes: chain of pointer-to-pointer hops (only shape handled; plain labels interleaved between hops are counted only by the hop counter)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Total decoded name length is not bounded inside the loop: after each backward hop, labels are read forward without limit and only rejected afterwards by Name() via _validate_labels (255 bytes), so each name can still read up to about 17 x message-size label bytes before it is rejected.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and fix are about pointer chain length; the length limit is 'already enforced' by NameTooLong at dns/name.py:356-357, so a solver would call it covered.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a gateway/relay-style rdata that decodes an embedded compressed name with its own small label/pointer loop instead of parser.get_name
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Gateway and Relay already special-case name-vs-address decoding by type, so a maintainer could plausibly have inlined a name reader there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an SvcParam (e.g. a DoH path or name-list param) that decodes names with a private decompressing loop
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SvcParam values have their own per-key from_wire_parser classes that parse sub-structures independently of dns.name.

O9_family: algorithmic complexity / uncontrolled recursion-like iteration in DNS name decompression (CWE-674)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a hop counter (or visited-offset set) in the pointer branch of dns/name.py:1157-1162, which is exactly the published fix.

out_of_scope_notes: Repeated full decompression of many names per message (no per-message decompression cache) is a separate quadratic-cost concern in dns/message.py:1128-1152; not pursued.
unverified: Repo size in MB not measured.

single_site red flag is applied even though one weak O8 route is listed: that route is in the same function, is mitigated by the 16-hop limit, and is arguably a different property (length, not chain depth).
Whether the 16-hop limit fully removes the residual per-name label-reading cost was not quantified (no code run).
